LESSON: DANGEROUS CHEMICALS AT HOME

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Safety Education
Topic 4.4: Dangerous chemicals at home

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dangerous chemicals at home. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya
3. practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps
4. apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DANGEROUS CHEMICALS AT HOME
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dangerous chemicals at home helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: DANGEROUS CHEMICALS AT HOME
Study Dangerous chemicals at home like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangerous chemicals at home” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Dangerous chemicals at home matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dangerous chemicals at home this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangerous chemicals at home” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dangerous chemicals at home is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangerous chemicals at home” around your school. (skill: explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Dangerous chemicals at home matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dangerous chemicals at home this week. (skill: practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangerous chemicals at home” around your school. (skill: apply Dangerous chemicals at home in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dangerous chemicals at home to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Dangerous chemicals at home in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Dangerous chemicals at home from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dangerous chemicals at home: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Dangerous chemicals at home?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dangerous chemicals at home means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Dangerous chemicals at home means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Dangerous chemicals at home from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
